NOP.description: No Operation - Does nothing for one instruction cycle.

NOP2.description: No Operation - Occupies 2 bytes, can be used for instruction alignment or timing adjustments.

NOP4.description: No Operation - Occupies 4 bytes, can be used for instruction alignment or timing adjustments.

NOP8.description: No Operation - Occupies 8 bytes, can be used for instruction alignment or timing adjustments.

LEA.description: Load Effective Address - Calculates the effective address: DRG = SR1 + (SR2 * Scale) + Offset.

MOV.description: Move - Copy the value from the source register to the destination register.

IMMB.description: Immediate Move Byte - Load an 8-bit immediate value into the destination register.

IMMW.description: Immediate Move Word - Load a 16-bit immediate value into the destination register.

IMMDW.description: Immediate Move Double Word - Load a 32-bit immediate value into the destination register.

FMOV.description: Floating Point Move - Copy the value from the source floating-point register to the destination floating-point register.

ADD.description: Add - Adds the values of two source registers and stores the result in the destination register.

SUB.description: Subtract - Subtracts the value of the second source register from the first source register and stores the result in the destination register.

SAR.description: Shift Arithmetic Right - Shifts the bits of the source register to the right by the number of positions specified in the second source register, preserving the sign bit, and stores the result in the destination register.

NEG.description: Negate - Computes the two's complement (negation) of the source register and stores the result in the destination register.

INC.description: Increment - Increases the value of the source register by one and stores the result in the destination register.

DEC.description: Decrement - Decreases the value of the source register by one and stores the result in the destination register.

SHL.description: Shift Left - Shifts the bits of the source register to the left by the number of positions specified in the second source register and stores the result in the destination register.

SHR.description: Shift Right - Shifts the bits of the source register to the right by the number of positions specified in the second source register and stores the result in the destination register.

XOR.description: Exclusive OR - Performs a bitwise exclusive OR operation between two source registers and stores the result in the destination register.

AND.description: AND - Performs a bitwise AND operation between two source registers and stores the result in the destination register.

OR.description: OR - Performs a bitwise OR operation between two source registers and stores the result in the destination register.

PUSH.description: Push - Push the value from the specified register onto the stack, and automatically adjust the stack pointer by bit-width (in Hayneko_arch32S, it is 32-bit).

POP.description: Pop - Pop the top value from the stack into the specified register, and automatically adjust the stack pointer by bit-width (in Hayneko_arch32S, it is 32-bit).

PUSHIP.description: Push Instruction Pointer - Push the current value of the instruction pointer onto the stack, and automatically adjust the stack pointer by bit-width (in Hayneko_arch32S, it is 32-bit).

IN.description: Input from Port - Read bit-length (in Hayneko_arch32S, it is 32-bit) of data from the specified I/O port into the destination register.

OUT.description: Output to Port - Write bit-length (in Hayneko_arch32S, it is 32-bit) of data from the source register to the specified I/O port.

LD.description: Load - Load a value from memory into the destination register using the address calculated from the base register and offset.

ST.description: Store - Store a value from the source register into memory using the address calculated from the base register and offset.

ISYSCALL.description: Interrupt System Call - Invokes an interrupt handler to request a service from the operating system.

SYSCALL.description: System Call - Invokes a system call and trigger interrupt 8 (#UI) to request a service from the operating system.

INT.description: Software Interrupt - Triggers a software interrupt to invoke an interrupt handler.

IRET.description: Interrupt Return - Returns from an interrupt handler to the point where the interrupt occurred.

HALT.description: Halt - Pauses the CPU until the next external interrupt is received.

REX.description: Register Extension Prefix - if any bits in the REX prefix are set, the instruction extends that register fields to allow access 16-31 of the 32-bit general-purpose registers.

BRH_H.description: Branch Hint Prefix - provides a hint to the processor about the likely direction of a branch instruction to optimize instruction pipelining. Must be used before a branch instruction, or the hint is ignored.

IOR.description: Instruction Length Override Prefix - explicitly specifies the length of the following instruction, overriding the default length determined by the opcode (can extend up to 16 bytes, not including prefixes).

OPC.description: Opcode field, specifies the operation to be performed by the processor.

SOP.description: Sub-Opcode field, specifies a variant of the main opcode operation.

ISL.description: Instruction Size Length field, specifies the length of the instruction in bytes.

DRG.description: Destination Register field, specifies the register where the result of the operation is stored.

SR1.description: Source Register 1 field, specifies the first source register for the operation.

SR2.description: Source Register 2 field, specifies the second source register for the operation.

SR3.description: Source Register 3 field, specifies the third source register for the operation.

DFR.description: Destination Floating-point Register field, specifies the floating-point register where the result of the operation is stored.

SF1.description: Source Floating-point Register 1 field, specifies the first source floating-point register for the operation.

SF2.description: Source Floating-point Register 2 field, specifies the second source floating-point register for the operation.

SF3.description: Source Floating-point Register 3 field, specifies the third source floating-point register for the operation.

IM8.description: Immediate field, specifies a constant value or address for the operation.

I16.description: Immediate field, specifies a constant value or address for the operation.

I32.description: Immediate field, specifies a constant value or address for the operation.

OF8.description: Offset field, specifies an offset value for memory access.

O16.description: Offset field, specifies an offset value for memory access.

O32.description: Offset field, specifies an offset value for memory access.

AD8.description: Address field, specifies an address for memory access.

A16.description: Address field, specifies an address for memory access.

A32.description: Address field, specifies an address for memory access.

SCL.description: Scale field, specifies the scaling factor for indexed addressing.

PRT.description: Port field, specifies the I/O port to be accessed.

CR.description: Control Register field, specifies the system control register to be accessed.

~DE.description: Divide Error - Triggered when a division by zero or overflow occurs during integer division.

#UD.description: Invalid Opcode Error - Triggered when an invalid or undefined opcode is encountered during instruction decoding.

#PF.description: Page Fault - Triggered when a memory access violation occurs, such as accessing a non-present page or violating access permissions.

#SO.description: Stack Overflow - Triggered when a stack overflow condition is detected, such as exceeding the stack size limit.

#GP.description: General Protection Fault - Triggered when a protection violation occurs, such as accessing restricted memory or executing privileged instructions in user mode.

*DF.description: Double Fault - Triggered when a second exception occurs while trying to service a prior exception, often indicating a serious system error.

#NC.description: Non-Maskable Interrupt - A high-priority interrupt that cannot be ignored by the processor, typically used for critical hardware events.

#II.description: Invalid Interrupt - Triggered when an invalid interrupt vector is encountered during interrupt handling.

#UI.description: User Interrupt - A software-generated interrupt used for user-level interrupt handling.

#TS.description: Timer Interrupt - Triggered by the system timer to manage time-related tasks.

#AC.description: Alignment Check Error - Triggered when a memory access violates the alignment requirements of the processor.

~MOUSE_INT.description: Mouse Interrupt - Triggered by mouse input events.

~KEYBOARD_INT.description: Keyboard Interrupt - Triggered by keyboard input events.

#SERIAL_INT.description: Serial Interrupt - Triggered by serial input events.

#DISK_INT.description: Disk Interrupt - Triggered by disk input events.

*MC.description: Machine Check - Triggered when the CPU detects a hardware error that cannot be corrected, such as memory errors or cache errors.

*FTLAB.description: Fatal Abort - Triggered when another fatal error occurs while handling Double Fault or CPU had detected a hardware fault, this will immediately reset the CPU.

ZF.description: Zero Flag - Set if the result of an operation is zero.

CF.description: Carry Flag - Set if an arithmetic operation generates a carry out or borrow into the most significant bit.

OF.description: Overflow Flag - Set if an arithmetic operation results in a signed overflow.

NF.description: Negative Flag - Set if the result of an operation is negative.

DF.description: Direction Flag - Controls the direction of string operations (0 = increment, 1 = decrement).

IF.description: Interrupt Flag - Controls the enabling and disabling of maskable interrupts.

BE.description: Big Endian Flag - Set if the processor is using a big-endian byte order.

AC.description: Alignment Check Flag - Enables alignment checking for memory accesses.

BH.description: Branch Hint Flag - Indicates the likely direction of a branch instruction for optimization purposes. (1 = taken, 0 = not taken)

XTE.description: XTU Enable Flag - Indicates whether the Extension Unit (XTU) is enabled.

BME.description: BMU Enable Flag - Indicates whether the Big Math Unit (BMU) is enabled.

MME.description: MMU Enable Flag - Indicates whether the Memory Management Unit (MMU) is enabled.

FPE.description: FPU Enable Flag - Indicates whether the Floating Point Unit (FPU) is enabled.

VIE.description: Virtual mode Interrupt Enable Flag - Indicates whether virtual mode interrupts are enabled.

architecture.name: Hayneko_Arch32S
architecture.description: Hayneko_Arch32S is a 32-bit RISC-like architecture with a Harvard architecture design, supporting floating-point operations. It is designed for efficient performance.

coprocessor.name: FPU
coprocessor.description: Floating Point Unit for handling floating-point operations.

coprocessor.name: XTU
coprocessor.description: Extension Unit for handling additional and complex instructions.

coprocessor.name: BMU
coprocessor.description: Big Math Unit for handling complex mathematical operations.

coprocessor.name: MMU
coprocessor.description: Memory Management Unit for handling memory management operations.

coprocessor.name: KCU
coprocessor.description: Kernel Control Unit for handling kernel and system-level operations.

pipelining.description: The architecture employs a 7-stage pipeline to enhance instruction throughput and overall performance.

out_of_order_execution.description: Supports out-of-order execution to improve performance by allowing instructions to be processed as resources become available rather than strictly in the order they appear in the instruction stream. Hayneko_Arch32S does not support out-of-order execution yet.

virtual_memory.description: Supports virtual memory with a page size of 4KB and uses a two-level paging mechanism for address translation.

L0.description: User mode for executing user applications with restricted access to system resources.

L2.description: Kernel mode for executing operating system code with full access to system resources.

L3.description: Hardware mode for direct hardware access and control, typically used for firmware and low-level system tasks.

L4.description: Hypervisor mode for managing virtual machines and providing virtualization services.

L7.description: Platform Secure mode for handling secure operations and sensitive data, providing an additional layer of security. It Has individual instruction set and system control.

interger.all: Free access in all modes (except ip, read-only in L0)

x0.description: Zero register, always holds the value 0.

ra.description: Return Address register, holds the return address for function calls.

rb.description: Base register, used for base addressing.

rc.description: Counter register, used for loop counting.

rd.description: Data register, used for general data storage.

ri.description: Index register, used for indexed addressing.

bp.description: Base Pointer register, used for stack frame management.

sp.description: Stack Pointer register, points to the top of the stack.

control.all: only accessible in kernel mode or hardware mode, user-mode denied

cr0.description: Control Register 0 - Used for system control and configuration.

cr1.description: Control Register 1 - Used for memory management and protection.

cr2.description: Control Register 2 - Used for interrupt handling and status.

cr3.description: Control Register 3 - Used for system performance monitoring.

kernel.all: only accessible in kernel mode or hardware mode, user-mode denied

mode.description: Kernel Mode Register - Indicates the current operating mode.

status.description: Kernel Status Register - Holds status flags and information.

ip.description: Program Counter Register - Holds the address of the next instruction to be executed. Can be modified in kernel mode or hardware mode.

idt.description: Interrupt Descriptor Table Register - Points to the interrupt descriptor table used for handling interrupts.

pm.description: Privilege Mode Register - Indicates the current privilege level of the processor.
